trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller may read the constellation device catalogue is decided per-handler by utils.CheckPermissions(w, req, PERM_LOGIN) at the top of constellation.DevicePublicList; at the pinned commit that handler instead only required a non-empty Authorization header (any string passed, and the stripped value was never used), and the /cosmos mux middleware does not reject a request that carries no jwttoken cookie, so an anonymous request with 'Authorization: Bearer anything' reached the full list of non-blocked, non-invisible devices (names, nicknames, IPs, hostnames, ports).

landing_point.why: The summary names the constellation public-devices endpoint and nothing else, so an engineer searches for that route and lands on DevicePublicList in this one file; the route registration at src/httpServer.go:690 and the swagger @Router annotation at src/constellation/api_devices_public.go:35 both point here.

fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP API handler, constellation package (mux srapiAdmin subrouter)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other route into this catalogue is the NATS subject cosmos._global_.constellation.public-devices, which is served over the cluster bus where every client is an admin-provisioned device user (per-device username/API-key password), so a solver reads it as cluster-internal machinery rather than the public HTTP endpoint, and there is no http.Request there to run CheckPermissions on.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Any logged-in user must keep seeing all visible devices: the built-in USER role holds only PERM_LOGIN/PERM_LOGIN_WEAK, and CheckPermissions short-circuits PERM_LOGIN to success for every API token. A fix that demands PERM_RESOURCES_READ/PERM_RESOURCES, or copies DeviceList's admin branch, would return only the caller's own devices (or nothing) for ordinary users, and would break existing SDK API tokens that carry no resource permissions.

no Authorization header at all (already rejected at the pin, api_devices_public.go:45-48)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-device variant such as GET /api/constellation/public-devices/{id} that projects a single PublicDeviceInfo
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The go-sdk already speaks this endpoint family (go-sdk/client.gen.go:7123) and the file already copy-pastes the whole projection into a second handler; a maintainer adding a single-device call for the SDK or an agent node would copy DevicePublicList including its header-presence check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third transport copy of the same projection (another NATS subject, e.g. .../public-devices/{name}, or a tunnel-facing route) bound to the same devices query
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The repo's own idiom in this file is to duplicate the handler body verbatim between transports (HTTP and NATS); a third copy that forgets the new CheckPermissions call is an obvious maintainer slip and would be found only by reading past the fixed handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a branch-free 'public view' flag on DeviceList that returns the limited projection for non-admins
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DeviceList already has the admin/non-admin split and the limited PublicDeviceInfo projection exists next to it in another file of the same package; folding the public view into it is a natural refactor that would move the decision away from the fixed handler.
